thread.title: Analysts Play Limbo With Apple Stock Price Targets | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Analysts Play Limbo With Apple Stock Price Targets | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Morgan Stanley on Friday slashed its price target on Apple stock, becoming the latest investment bank to lower the bar for the consumer electronics giant.
X Analyst Katy Huberty cut her target on Apple ( AAPL ) to 236 from 253, but kept her overweight rating. Apple stock dropped 3.6% to 168.49 on the stock market today .
Since hitting an all-time high of 233.47 on Oct. 3, Apple stock has tumbled 27.8% through Friday's close. The swift drop has made Apple's brief flirtation with a $1 trillion market cap a distant memory, and left Wall Street analysts struggling to adjust their price targets.
Huberty lowered her iPhone unit sales estimate for Apple's fiscal 2019 to reflect a weakening China smartphone market. Demand is particularly soft for high-end handsets, where Apple plays, she said in a report to clients.

Huberty cut her iPhone sales estimate for fiscal 2019 to 200 million units from 213 million units. That would translate to an 8% decline in unit sales over fiscal 2018, which ended Sept. 29.
She sees wearables and services helping to offset the iPhone weakness. Wearables include the Apple Watch, AirPods wireless earbuds and Beats headphones. Services include the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare, iCloud and other offerings.
Other Apple Stock Target Cuts She predicts Apple revenue will rise 4% year over year to $277 billion in fiscal 2019 thanks to wearables, services and higher average selling prices for iPhones.
On Thursday, Rosenblatt Securities cut its price target on Apple stock to 165 from 200 and reiterated its neutral rating.
On Tuesday, HSBC downgraded Apple to hold from buy and trimmed its 12-month price target to 200 from 205.
